static_traits.name: Fang Ming
static_traits.occupation: Currently employed; looking for a second job
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with fellow-runner friends strained by a negative mindset toward own running ability; has a few supportive friends, but has not yet discussed own unease and inadequacy with them.
static_traits.medical_history: Has not yet received treatment for psychological problems; no significant physical illness or important prior history.
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic, able to self-reflect and cooperate; positive attitude, but with marked self-denial and a tendency to compare with others.

basic_info.main_problem: In recent months, I have felt persistent self-doubt about running, though running is a hobby I love. As I hope to improve my running level, this inadequacy feels stronger. Comparing with other runners in the community leaves me moderately stressed; every run seeing others overtake me is depressing, to the point I no longer get joy from running. I have tried different training plans and techniques, but without significant progress.
basic_info.core_demands: These feelings of inadequacy are starting to affect my overall enjoyment of running and undermining my motivation to pursue the dream of 'opening a restaurant that incorporates running', so I decided to seek counseling.

core_beliefs: I am not a good runner

special_situations.event: Seeing other runners faster and passing me when running in the community
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I can't run as fast as them or at least keep up, it means I am not good enough, not a good runner
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Intensifying training, trying different training plans to prove myself

special_situations.event: After running, friends give positive feedback, pointing out I am improving
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only higher objective results or rankings count as 'progress'; others' praise isn't reliable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive feedback, focusing only on own inadequacy
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They're just comforting me; this isn't real progress

special_situations.event: Before running, thinks of possibly seeing faster runners on the track
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I can't reach their level, continuing to run is meaningless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Skips running and reduces training to avoid frustration and shame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can't catch up with them anyway, so why run?

special_situations.event: When reviewing recent training logs, only noticing the poor-performing sessions
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Negative performance more truly reflects my level; positive experiences are just chance
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores good running experiences and positive data, strengthens attention to negative evidence
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My overall performance is poor; those few good times were just luck

core_conflict.wish: Longing to gain recognition and a sense of achievement through running, and to feel valuable
core_conflict.fear: Fearing appearing not good enough after comparison, being belittled or rejected, the dream frustrated by own inadequacy
defense_goal: Maintaining control and proving myself through doubling training and continuous comparison
Reduces shame and frustration by skipping runs and distancing himself from running friends

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or friends give positive feedback and encourage them to attend to their own progress and positive evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to understand others' positive evaluation as 'just comfort', struggling to believe positive evidence (transference: distrust of others' recognition)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Hesitant tone, downplaying positive evidence, repeatedly starting with 'but/however' to emphasize inadequacy, diluting positive experiences.

manifestations: Running gradually losing its fun and meaning
Every time he runs and sees others pass him, he feels frustrated
Not yet discussing inner inadequacy and unease with supportive friends
outcomes: Social support not yet effectively utilized
Sense of isolation and increased self-doubt

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently evaluating self as 'I am not good enough'
Negating others' positive feedback and own good experiences
Reinforcing self-blame and self-doubt after comparing with others

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Choosing to skip runs when anticipating frustration, to avoid directly facing the stimulus
Not expressing own inadequacy and unease to supportive friends

exception_events.target_problem: When running with the community, the client typically feels low self-esteem and frustration from comparing with faster runners, then loses motivation and occasionally skips training
exception_events.unique_outcome: On a few runs, the client subjectively felt in good shape, strong and capable, able to complete the session; friends also reported improvement after the run
exception_events.reason: Different support: friends gave positive feedback after the run; different experience cues: subjectively feeling stronger and more in control during the run

positive_force: Once had a 'strong / capable' running experience and enjoyed running
Willing to seek counseling and has a positive attitude
Current work performance satisfactory, with a certain stability and execution ability
negative_force: Habitual comparison with others leading to self-denial
Negating positive feedback and positive experiences
Cognitive distortions like personalization and mental filtering reinforcing the sense of frustration
Decreased motivation and avoiding training by skipping runs
Sleep and overall motivation affected by negative emotions

target_behavior.behavior: Shows self-deprecation in running-related situations and avoids training (skips running)
antecedent: Every time going out for a run
When seeing other community runners pass them
Before running, thinking about one's stagnant progress or others being faster
target_behavior.core_reason: Driven by the core belief 'I am not good enough / not a good runner' and cognitive distortions of comparison and despair, mental filtering, and disqualifying the positive, to avoid shame and frustration
target_behavior.function: Escaping unwelcome emotions (shame, frustration), lowering anxiety short-term and protecting self-esteem
target_behavior.consequence: Losing the fun and drive of running, relationship tension, sleep and daily energy affected

target_behavior.behavior: Negating positive feedback and signs of self-progress
antecedent: When friends give positive evaluations or point out one's progress
When reviewing training records that include both good and bad performances
target_behavior.core_reason: Lacking a secure sense of self-worth, with cognitive distortions of 'disqualifying the positive' and 'mental filtering'
target_behavior.function: Maintains a negative self-schema to avoid expectations and the disappointment that comes with them
target_behavior.consequence: Confidence hard to build, persistent self-denial, further lowering training motivation
